findings.title: The tiny measure within moral counsel
findings.claim: Luqman's nearby warning against shirk and statement that the return is to God let the focus's mustard-seed weight carry a contextual echo of moral responsibility, while it remains a literal measure.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier مِثْقَالَ (31:16:5:1) fixes the seed's tiny physical weight. The supplied 31:13 text calls shirk a great wrongdoing, and 31:14 says the return is to God. Those moral and return cues meet the focus root's sin-burden branch, so the measured weight can also suggest a small wrong borne as responsibility.
findings.reader_payoff: A thing too small to notice can still carry moral weight within the same counsel that warns against wrongdoing and says the return is to God.
findings.containment: This is an attributed contextual resonance: the focus does not explicitly name a sin or deed, and the return is not described as a specific reckoning or punishment. Its tiny physical measure remains intact, and the referent of the feminine pronoun is not resolved here.

epistemic.reason: The focus occurrence and both context texts are exact in the packet. The moral-burden relation is inferential because 31:16 does not name a sin or deed and 31:14 does not specify a reckoning.

findings.title: The seed meets the language of love
findings.claim: The focus's حَبَّةٍ remains a seed-grain, while the pericope's statement that Allah does not love arrogance activates the root's love branch as a restrained contextual echo.
findings.mechanism: The focus word حَبَّةٍ at 31:16:6:1 is the grain carrier, and its focus analysis preserves affection as a contextual echo. The supplied Arabic of 31:18 contains لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخْتَالٍ فَخُورٍ, an independent love cue in the same moral counsel. That contact lets the seed word touch the love branch while retaining its ordinary grain meaning.
findings.reader_payoff: The small grain and the later statement about what Allah does not love become linked within Luqman's moral instruction, adding an affective edge to the concrete image without turning it into another word.
findings.containment: This does not claim that حَبَّةٍ means love here, that Allah loves the grain, or that 31:16 speaks about arrogance. The 31:18 Arabic is supplied without target-side morphology or lexical analysis, so the cross-ayah root link remains qualified.

epistemic.reason: The focus root and its affection-related contextual note are supplied, and 31:18 provides exact Arabic for the love cue. The target-side morphology and root mapping are absent, so the cross-ayah activation is qualified.

findings.title: The aware one and those who dispute without knowledge
findings.claim: The focus's closing Khabīr can be heard against the pericope's later mention of people disputing about Allah without knowledge, giving the attribute a human counterpoint beyond the hidden grain itself.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier خَبِيرٌ (31:16:24:1) closes the retrieval statement with complete inner awareness. In 31:20, the exact target text describes some people as disputing about Allah without knowledge, after naming blessings both apparent and hidden. The knowledge cue meets the focus's knowledge branch and contrasts divine awareness with human uninformed argument.
findings.reader_payoff: Khabīr becomes not only a seal on the hidden thing's retrieval but also a contrast between divine awareness and human claims about God that lack knowledge.
findings.containment: This does not claim that 31:20 explains the grain or its retrieval; the connection note explicitly limits that relation. The target morphology is unavailable, and this is a qualified pericope-level contrast, not a formal syntactic link or a claim about every dispute.

epistemic.reason: The focus carrier and target Arabic are exact, but the focus branch identity is qualified and the target-side morphology is absent. The contrast is a contextual inference.

findings.title: Mercy colors subtle reach
findings.claim: The host basmala's names of mercy frame the focus's Laṭīf as gentle, careful reach: Allah's access to what is hidden can be heard as care as well as fine-grained ability.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier لَطِيفٌ (31:16:23:1) closes the retrieval statement with subtle divine access. The automatic host context 31:0 names Allah as al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm. Because both contexts name the same divine agent, the basmala's explicit mercy supplies an independent trigger for the focus root's branch of gentle, careful action.
findings.reader_payoff: The hidden thing is not only within divine reach; the host opening lets that reach carry a tone of gentleness and care.
findings.containment: This is a contextual resonance across distinct roots, not a lexical equation of mercy with Laṭīf. The focus states subtle access and retrieval, not an explicit motive or a changed referent for the hidden thing.

epistemic.reason: Both the host basmala and focus attribute are supplied exactly, and the focus branch is accepted. The caring frame is an interpretive relation across distinct roots, not an explicit paraphrase of the focus.
